**Subject: Tuesday reading club at Knocknacarra**

Dear Niamh,

I’ve been thinking about your email of 30 October, and I wanted to send you an update on the Tuesday reading club before our review meeting on Wednesday 18 November.

The club has been running in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library since September 2025. We had five children most weeks in September, but numbers have been building: nine by mid-October, and fourteen last Tuesday, 3 November. It’s a lovely change to see, and I’m thrilled the club seems to be finding its feet.

There have been some especially heartening moments. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined in October, and the older one now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. One boy who wouldn’t open a book back in September asked last week if he could take two home. Salthill Book Nook has also kindly donated 120 books, mostly for ages six to nine, with a good few as Gaeilge. It has made a real difference to have fresh books for the children to choose from.

I know the pause from January was proposed because attendance was low and the hall insurance is going up. Given how the numbers have changed, would you be willing to look at the latest attendance figures before the 18th and reconsider the pause? I’d hate to see the club stopped just as it seems to be taking off.

I also need to tell you about something I should have handled differently. I met Orla Keane, a reporter with the Corrib Courier, at the farmers’ market. I got carried away talking about the club and told her she could come along any Tuesday. She would like to visit on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer. I know visits and photographs need to go through you first, and that no children can be photographed without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I was wrong not to check with you before saying anything, plain and simple.

The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it’s done properly. I’m happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve had a chance to decide. If you’re comfortable with it going ahead, I can also collect the consent forms myself, as you direct.

I hope the new numbers and the children’s progress will help with your review. Thank you for all you do to coordinate the volunteers and support the club. I’d be very glad to talk it through before the meeting if that would be useful.

Warm regards,  
[Your name]
